Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli
 Order

The present appeal under Section 173 of The Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 preferred by the insurer assails the award dated 03.06.2022 passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, not only qua the quantum of compensation but also qua the non-grant of recovery rights against the driver and owner of the insured vehicle.
2.

As already noted in the order dated 17.01.2023, the respondent no 1 to 6, who were the claimants before the Tribunal, are concerned only with the grievance of the appellant qua the quantum of compensation awarded towards future prospects, which it is the appellant's plea, was required to be increased by 25% of the annual income of the deceased, has been the erroneously increased by 30%
by the learned Tribunal.

In so far as the grievance of the appellant qua non-grant of recovery rights against the owner and/or the driver of the insured vehicle is concerned, it is only respondent no. 7 and 8 who are the affected parties.

3. After the matter was heard at some length on 17.01.2023 and this court was, prima facia, inclined to accept the appellant's plea that future prospects were required to be computed by computing 25%
of the income towards future prospects of the deceased as against 30% considered by the learned Tribunal, the learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 6, on the said date, had prayed for time to obtain instructions.

sentences.text: Today, learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 6 submits, on instructions, that taking into account that the claimants have been waiting to receive compensation since 20.03.2016, when the accident took place, they are agreeable that the future prospects be reduced to 25%.

5. In the light of the aforesaid stand taken by the learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 6, while vacating the interim order dated 13.09.2022, the impugned order is modified by directing that instead of 30% addition, as directed under para 28 of the impugned award, the compensation towards the future prospects would be computed by taking 25% of the income of the deceased.

Consequently, after adding 25% to the monthly income of Rs. 7864/- of the deceased and deducting 1/3rd amount towards his personal expenses therefrom, the net monthly contribution towards deceased towards his family works out of Rs. 6554/-.

Resultantly, the amount payable towards "loss of dependency" would stand reduced to Rs. 10,22,424/- (Rs 6554 x 12x13) as against Rs. 11,16,336/-
granted by the Tribunal.
The awarded amount will therefore stand reduce by Rs. 93,912/-, entitling the Respondent 1 to 6 to receive a sum of Rs. 12,124/- along with interest at rate of 6% in terms of the impugned award.

6. Since the appellant has already deposited the entire awarded amount with the learned Tribunal,
the Tribunal is directed to release the amount, in terms of this order, in favour of the claimants along with accrued interest thereon, as per the disbursal scheme contained in the award.
The differential amount of Rs. 93,912/- along with accrued interest be released in favour of the appellant.

7. In view of this order and the stand taken by the respondent no 1 to 6, the appellant's claim against the respondent nos.1 to 6 does not survive any further and, therefore, they need not appear in the appeal, which will now be proceeded only qua the respondent nos.7 & 8, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle, who are still unserved.
8. However, since none appears for respondent no. 7 and 8, upon the appellant taking steps, issue notice to the respondent nos.7 & 8 through all permissible modes.

REKHA PALLI, J JANUARY 18, 2023 sr Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Ram Kali Yadav & Ors on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125712097/
